question: Amit invests a sum of ₹5400 and Gopal invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Gopal gets ₹600 more interest than Amit, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Difference in Simple Interest for 5 years = ₹600

Simple Interest on the difference for 1 year = ₹600 ÷ 5 = ₹120

Rate % = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Difference in Principal) × 100

Rate % = (120 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 3%

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Amit: ₹5400
 
 
 Gopal: ₹9400

 

 

 

 
 
 Difference: ₹4000
 Extra SI = ₹600

 SI on ₹4000 for 5 years = ₹600

**Given:**

Principal for Amit (P₁) = ₹5400

Principal for Gopal (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 5 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹600

Let the rate of interest be R% per annum.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI of Gopal − SI of Amit = ₹600

⇒ [(P₂ × R × T) ÷ 100] − [(P₁ × R × T) ÷ 100] = 600

⇒ [(P₂ − P₁) × R × T] ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ [(9400 − 5400) × R × 5] ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ (4000 × R × 5) ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ 20000R ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ 200R = 600

⇒ R = 600 ÷ 200

⇒ R = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. The interest earned remains constant for every year if the rate and principal are unchanged. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Difference in Simple Interest

When the interest rate and time period are the same, the difference in interest earned on two distinct principal amounts is exactly equal to the simple interest calculated on the difference between those principals.

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike Simple Interest, Compound Interest is calculated on the initial principal as well as the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: Amount = P × (1 + R/100)T.
